title: Floating LNG's growing role in unlocking the next generation of global gas supply
gist: This is a Gastech-linked gated-content teaser (download-form page), not a full analytical article; its only disclosed content is the framing thesis that floating LNG (FLNG) is entering a new growth phase as project economics, development models and global supply priorities evolve, unlocking frontier gas resources that conventional onshore projects cannot reach. The bulleted list describes the scope of a gated report rather than disclosed findings.

insights.claim: Floating LNG (FLNG) is entering a new growth phase driven by evolving project economics, development models, and global supply priorities.
insights.speaker: Fraser Carson
insights.so_what: Investors tracking global LNG supply growth should treat FLNG as a rising, not marginal, supply category as conventional project economics shift.
insights.quote: Floating LNG is entering a new chapter.

insights.claim: FLNG is positioned to play an increasingly important role in unlocking new sources of gas supply and bringing frontier gas resources to market that would otherwise remain stranded.
insights.speaker: Fraser Carson
insights.so_what: Frontier/stranded gas resources previously uneconomic for onshore liquefaction become investable once FLNG capacity and cost curves improve — watch for FIDs on remote/offshore gas fields.
insights.quote: FLNG could play an increasingly important role in unlocking new sources of supply and bringing frontier gas resources to market.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie identifies floating liquefaction as capable of creating development opportunities in locations or project settings that conventional (onshore) LNG projects cannot access.
insights.speaker: Fraser Carson
insights.so_what: Where onshore LNG trains are economically or logistically blocked, FLNG is the structural workaround — a key differentiator for evaluating which resource plays get developed next.
insights.quote: Where floating liquefaction can create opportunities that conventional projects cannot

insights.claim: The commercial case for FLNG is shifting because costs, project timelines, and commercial/contracting models are all evolving simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Fraser Carson
insights.so_what: A multi-dimensional cost/timeline/commercial-model shift suggests FLNG project economics could improve faster than headline capex figures alone would indicate.
insights.quote: How costs, timelines and commercial models are evolving
